message.abstract: <jats:p>This work evaluates the accumulated dose at a High Bandwidth Memory (HBM)-relevant location during printed circuit board (PCB) X-ray inspection under real manufacturing conditions. Measurements used an Omron VT-X750 3D CT X-ray inspection system at 115 kV and 130 μA with 1 mm Al filtration. A silicon PIN diode dosimeter at selected HBM locations recorded the dose rate and accumulated dose during the inspection scan. HBM-relevant exposure was strongly affected by PCB attenuation, HBM/package attenuation, scan position, and backscatter. The 3 mm PCB reduced the dose rate by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the direct-beam reference, and the additional HBM attenuation corresponded to an effective Cu thickness of approximately 0.15–0.16 mm. After PCB transmission, most of the remaining exposure was attenuated in the HBM/package structure. Combining this estimate with the image-sensor-side backscatter gives an HBM-relevant exposure estimate of approximately 75% of the PCB-transmitted exposure (average dose-rate equivalent approximately 0.46 mGy(Si)/s), an operational value derived from detector-dose differences rather than a measured absorbed dose in the HBM dies. The dose-rate waveform showed that exposure at the HBM location accumulates through transient events as the beam scans the PCB. HBM exposure during PCB X-ray inspection cannot be estimated from machine settings or static geometry alone; PCB/package attenuation, scan trajectory, component location, and backscatter must be considered.</jats:p>
title: Manufacturing-Process Dose Estimation for HBM During PCB X-Ray Inspection: Effects of PCB Attenuation, Package Structure, and Backscatter
